course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: General Physics for Data Science

primary.name: Prof. Chey Chan Oeurn Krem Sona

clos.description: Apply fundamental physics principles of motion, energy, wave, and electricity to interpret data generated from real-world sensing and measurement systems.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Midterm exam, Group Homework, Diagnostic Quiz

clos.description: Analyze environmental and climate-related physical systems by examining temperature humidity, energy, and resource-use data using physics-based reasoning.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Group Assignment, Group Homework, Diagnostic Quiz

clos.description: Present a scientifically structured technical report and oral presentation explaining the working principles and data interpretation of a selected physics-based device with professional responsibility.

continuousAssessmentRows: Group written report and Group presentation – CLO3

assessments.name: Group written report and Group presentation

topics.title: Topic 1: Course introduction; Units & Measurement
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Identify SI base and derived units used in sensing systems LLO2. Apply dimensional analysis to verify physical equations

topics.title: Topic 2: Errors, uncertainty & Linear regression
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Apply linear regression to determine physical parameters from sensor data LLO2. Interpret slope and intercept in physical context

topics.title: Topic 3: Position vector, Velocity, Acceleration
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Calculate velocity and acceleration from discrete datasets LLO2. Differentiate between average and instantaneous velocity

topics.title: Topic 4: Force
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Draw free-body diagrams for mechanical systems LLO2. Apply Newton’s Second Law to analyze motor-driven systems

topics.title: Topic 5: Work, Power, Efficiency
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Calculate mechanical and electrical power from real datasets LLO2. Determine system efficiency using input-output data

topics.title: Topic 6: Rotation of Rigid bodies
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Define angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration LLO2. Calculate torque and rotational kinetic energy

topics.title: Topic 7: Thermodynamics for climate change
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Explain temperature, heat, and internal energy concepts LLO2. Analyze energy transfer in atmospheric systems LLO3. Interpret temperature and humidity datasets using thermodynamic principles LLO4. Examine efficiency and entropy concepts in climate systems

topics.title: Topic 8: Electricity: current, voltage, resistance
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Define current, voltage, resistance LLO2. Apply Ohm’s Law to electrical datasets

topics.title: Topic 9: RC charging/discharging
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Calculate time constants from circuit parameters LLO2. Analyze voltage-time data to extract RC values

topics.title: Topic 10: Faraday’s Law & Electromagnetics induction
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Apply Faraday’s Law to generator systems LLO2. Interpret induced voltage signals from coils

topics.title: Topic 11: Inductors & transient behaviours
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Apply L/R time constant equations LLO2. Analyze transient current behavior from datasets

topics.title: Topic 12: Mini-Project
topics.llosRaw: LLO1. Select a physics-based device for investigation LLO2. Organize collected experimental data systematically LLO3. Prepare a structured technical report LLO4. Present findings clearly using scientific reasoning LLO5. Demonstrate responsible teamwork and data integrity

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
